solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: End of Clegg? Scope for game sacrifice

indicators.note: the end of a name points to its final letter only, discarding the rest of the word

blocks.note: Nick Clegg, former Lib Dem leader; his name ends in G
an ambit is the scope or extent of something

explanation.surface: A satirical jab: Nick Clegg's political career ends, his range reduced to a mere sacrifice in someone else's game.
explanation.walkthrough: Clegg sacrificed his party in coalition with Cameron, so the surface fits the definition neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess an opening that gives up a pawn for positional advantage is called by this name, hence a sacrifice in a game.

clue.text: (& 5dn.) Inflexible Miliband's lot, an unwelcome extra for the old time-server

definitions.text: an unwelcome extra for the old time-server

blocks.note: hard means rigid, not yielding
Ed Miliband led the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband's rigid Labour Party pictured as a tiresome burden on a weary veteran serving out his time.
explanation.walkthrough: A time-server here is a prisoner doing time; old sentences could add compulsory physical work on top of imprisonment.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically British courts could impose punishing physical toil alongside a prison sentence, an unpleasant addition for convicts.

clue.text: Drug user who sounds a nag?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who takes cocaine up the nose
second meaning: one who makes the noise a horse makes through its nostrils

explanation.surface: An addict whose speech is like the nagging of a scold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb about complaining, but it is an old horse, and the sound is the horse's.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who inhales powder through the nose, and also anyone making that loud nasal horse-like noise.

clue.text: To many, a ballsed-up members' division

indicators.note: something ballsed-up is botched and messed about, so the letters come out in a muddled order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside that, for most people, the split in a party's membership was a botched job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' means limbs, not party members; the word's Greek root means cutting up, so dissecting a body is the division.
explanation.definitionFit: The science originally meant dissection, the cutting apart of a body into its limbs and organs.

clue.text: see 2dn.
An element of a column: "Ever twisted round end of taut underwear?"

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of its usual shape, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter alone
round says the rearranged letters wrap about the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the final letter of taut
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: A tabloid quote about some columnist's twisted remark on tight lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The column is the spinal column, not a newspaper one; the jumbled letters wrap round the single letter before the underwear is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The backbone is built from a stack of small bones, each one a single segment of that spinal column.

clue.text: Monica's dress accessory catching Bill's head, which wouldn't increase the vote

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a participle describing someone not voting

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
catching means seizing hold of, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: Monica Lewinsky's blue dress famously bore a stain, here a staining
the opening letter of Bill, as in Clinton

explanation.surface: The Clinton-Lewinsky scandal: Monica's stained dress implicating Bill, an embarrassment hardly likely to win votes.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside A STAINING, just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from casting a ballot adds nothing to the tally for either side.

clue.text: (& 29ac./9ac.)Farage incidents that he distorted, being about to cross over to the other side?

definitions.text: being about to cross over to the other side?

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of true shape, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: all twenty-one letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage spinning stories about incidents, perhaps on the brink of defecting to another party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross over to the other side' suggests a political defection, but here it means dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing imminent mortality is like nearing the passage to the afterlife, a euphemism for death.

clue.text: see 8dn.
Blair's vacant 'three' irritated northern community members

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so the inside of the name is cleared out leaving its outer letters
irritated suggests stirred up and agitated, so the word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Blair
the word taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's empty talk of 'three' annoys a northern community.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old plural of brother, used for fellow members of a religious order or society.

clue.text: It's worse to cover Nigel's butt – relieved by peer

indicators.note: a butt is the tail end of something, so only the final letter of the name is kept
covering something means going around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: badder is a colloquial comparative of bad, meaning worse
the final letter of Nigel

explanation.surface: A political attack on Nigel Farage's backside being covered up, then rescued by a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: Peer is read as pee-er, someone who urinates; L sits inside BADDER after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: This organ fills with urine and is emptied whenever someone passes water, a joking reading of the noble title.

clue.text: Revolution not an option for those who voted

blocks.note: a turn is one revolution, a rotation
something that is out is ruled out, not on the table

explanation.surface: Revolution is no option for an electorate that chose to vote instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of electors actually casting ballots at an election is reported as this figure.

clue.text: Ultimate educational division? Not for a presumptuous Cameron

blocks.note: first meaning: the final part of a three-part school year
second meaning: a further spell in office David Cameron said he would not seek

explanation.walkthrough: Cameron announced before the 2015 election that he would not stand for a further stint as prime minister, which some called presumptuous since he had not yet won a second.
explanation.definitionFit: British school years are split into three periods, the last being the summer one; politically it is a third period in office.

clue.text: M'lud, Rice mangled a musical item

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so these letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe and comma ignored

explanation.surface: A courtroom address to the judge about some Rice who wrecked a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: M'lud is how barristers address a judge in a British court.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stringed instrument played by striking the strings with small hammers, so an item for making music.

clue.text: Heath-Robinson houses movingly manifest an erection

indicators.note: a building houses what is inside it, so the answer lies within the words

blocks.note: found across the hyphen, from the end of the first name into the second

explanation.surface: An absurdly elaborate Heath Robinson contraption that produces an erection.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist known for drawing ludicrously complicated machines.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulsate rhythmically, as an aroused member visibly does, beating with the pulse.

clue.text: Farage casually drinks gallons, live – "Bother!"

indicators.note: drinking takes something inside, so these letters swallow the following ones

blocks.note: Nige is the informal short form of Nigel, Farage's first name
G is the abbreviation for gallons
L marks the live wire in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage casually downing pints by the gallon, exclaiming in annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: G and L go inside NIGE, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor irritation or worry that nags at someone, the kind of trivial trouble meant by an exasperated exclamation.

clue.text: NATO manoeuvres bound to unite with East? That'll be the day!

indicators.note: manoeuvres are tactical repositionings, so the letters of the alliance are moved around

blocks.note: the alliance's letters rearranged
a hop is a small jump or bound
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: NATO military exercises bound to join up with the East: an unlikely prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are scornful exclamations meaning something will never happen, an expression of utter disbelief.

clue.text: Crown: Camilla's ultimate downhill course

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the name is used

blocks.note: a crest is the top or crown of something
the final letter of Camilla

explanation.surface: Camilla's hopes of the crown take a final downhill slide.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cresta Run is a famous toboggan run at St Moritz in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The run is an icy track in a Swiss resort on which riders slide head-first down the mountain.

clue.text: Express is after Sun, which is not to be sniffed at!

definitions.text: which is not to be sniffed at!

blocks.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
to vent a feeling is to express it

explanation.surface: A newspaper joke: the Express chasing the Sun, both tabloids not worth dismissing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Express and the Sun are British tabloids; 'not to be sniffed at' usually means worth having, but here glue-sniffing is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquids like glue thinners give off fumes abused by inhalers, so this is literally something one should not inhale.

clue.text: Squaddie at first beaten off, then paraded

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of squaddie
vulgar slang for masturbated

explanation.surface: A soldier is first beaten up and then marched on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: A squaddie is British slang for a private soldier, which suits 'paraded'.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off or swagger boastfully, as if displaying oneself on a parade ground.

clue.text: Cyclops is having sex with fed ape

blocks.note: the setter speaking: Cyclops is = I'm
it is a coy word for sex
ate means took food, fed

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of an encounter with a well-fed primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like the animal, but as a verb it means copy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic or copy their behaviour, the verb taken from monkeys' supposed copying.

clue.text: African people voice disapproval – militant group rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the short name runs back to front

blocks.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
IS stands for Islamic State

explanation.surface: A people tutting in disapproval while turning away a militant group.
explanation.definitionFit: This ethnic group lives mainly in Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: An Italian's 'nut-sac' nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the preceding letters go wild and are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crude remark about an Italian man's scrotum and testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'nuts' doubles as slang for testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Tuscany, the central Italian region around Florence, is an Italian of that kind.

clue.text: "Blow men!" is perverted form of it?

definitions.text: "Blow men!" is perverted form of it?

indicators.note: perverted means turned away from its proper form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneering joke that a crude slogan is a twisted version of a political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: 'it' is the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The feminist campaign for equality of the sexes, whose slogan a sexist might twist into a dismissal of the opposite gender.

clue.text: Put much effort into Fanny

blocks.note: first meaning: to work hard at something, like the industrious rodent
second meaning: vulgar slang for female genitals

explanation.surface: Someone putting a lot of effort into a woman named Fanny.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang fanny means the vulva, not the buttocks as in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: To work industriously is to toil like the dam-building animal; the noun is also coarse slang for pubic hair and genitals.

clue.text: Spilling the beans, no time for Gordon Brown now?

indicators.note: no means without, so a letter is taken away from the phrase
spilling scatters things about, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time, removed

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, out of office, revealing secrets in his memoirs with no time left.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was a British prime minister voted out in 2010.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose fame or power lies in the past, as a defeated former prime minister now is.

clue.text: Material that's gross, perverse cheesy stuff

indicators.note: perverse means turned the wrong way, so the word is read back to front

blocks.note: gross can mean obese, fat
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A fabric that is disgusting, warped and smelly like cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a crisp, lustrous woven silk or synthetic cloth used for dresses, so a type of fabric.

clue.text: (& 28ac.) The decent thing to do just before shag under piano

indicators.note: in a down entry, being under something means sitting below it, so the slang word goes after the musical abbreviation

blocks.note: just means fair, equitable
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
lay is slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that the decent thing is a quick tumble under the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'under piano' puts LAY below P; 'just' looks like 'only' but means fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest, sporting conduct that respects the rules is considered the proper and honourable way to behave.
